title.narrative: Theme 1: Integrated Response to Malnutrition (IRM) through Agriculture, Health, Nutrition, and WASH Interventions in Oromia Region, Kelem Wollega Zone, Dale Wabera and Gawo Kebe districts.

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtSOS Sahel Ethiopia, in partnership with HUNDEE—Oromo Grassroots Development Initiative and Women Empowerment—Action (WE-Action), proposes a one-year integrated, multisectoral humanitarian response in Dale Wabera and Dawo Kebe districts of Kelem Wollega zone, Oromia Region, targeting 23,145 people (12,504 female) affected by conflict, displacement, and compounding crises. The project addresses urgent needs across agriculture and livelihoods, WASH, health, and nutrition through a coordinated, inclusive, and context-appropriate approach emphasizing protection and accountability to affected populations (AAP).lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtIn the agriculture and livelihoods sector, the project targets 3,415 people to revitalize household food production and strengthen recovery. Activities include distributing certified seeds and farming tools, and livestock restocking with veterinary support. Vulnerable groups—internally displaced persons (IDPs), returnees, and host community members—will engage in poultry production, petty trade, vegetable gardening, apiculture, and homestead fruit cultivation to restore livelihoods, increase food security, and enhance resilience.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe WASH component targets 8,711 people and focuses on restoring access to clean and safe water through the rehabilitation of shallow wells, spring capping, and tap stands, as well as the repair and replacement of damaged water pipelines. Emergency latrines will be constructed and maintained in displacement sites and institutions. Hygiene promotion activities will include the distribution of WASH NFIs, environmental cleaning kits, and hygiene education campaigns, aimed at reducing waterborne diseases and improving community health.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtIn the health sector, 8,176 people will benefit from services delivered by Mobile Health and Nutrition Teams (MHNTs) in hard-to-reach communities. The teams will provide primary health care and integrate the Minimum Initial Service Package (MISP) for reproductive health. Vaccination campaigns will target children for preventable diseases, while Social and Behavior Change Communication (SBCC) will promote risk awareness and healthy practices. The project will also strengthen early warning and disease surveillance systems to support timely public health responses.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe nutrition component targets 2,843 people, focusing on the treatment of Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) and Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM) in children, along with targeted supplementary feeding for pregnant and lactating women (PLW). Interventions will include active malnutrition screening, last-mile distribution of nutrition commodities, and promotion of Infant and Young Child Feeding in Emergencies (IYCF-E) practices to mitigate malnutrition risks among vulnerable populations.ltbrgtCrosscutting priorities—gender equality, inclusion, protection mainstreaming, and AAP—will be fully integrated across all components. Special attention will be given to women, girls, older persons, and persons with disabilities. The project will emphasize community participation in planning and implementation, with robust feedback and complaint handling mechanisms to ensure transparency, responsiveness, and trust.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThis comprehensive response will not only meet life-saving needs but also contribute to early recovery and long-term community resilience. SOS Sahel Ethiopia and its partners are requesting USD 500,000 to implement this humanitarian intervention over 12 months, directly reaching 23,145 people (12,504 female)ltbrgtlt/pgt
